primary.title: The Analects
primary.author: Confucius
primary.rationale: The Analects is a collection of sayings and ideas attributed to the Chinese philosopher Confucius and his contemporaries, traditionally believed to have been compiled by Confucius's followers. It is the most famous and influential of the Four Books.

primary.title: The Great Learning
primary.author: Confucius
primary.rationale: The Great Learning is one of the Four Books in Confucian philosophy. It is a short, introductory text that outlines the path to self-cultivation and good governance.

primary.title: The Doctrine of the Mean
primary.author: Confucius
primary.rationale: The Doctrine of the Mean is another of the Four Books, focusing on the importance of balance, moderation, and harmony in personal conduct and governance.

secondary.title: Confucius: A Life of Thought
secondary.author: Benjamin I. Schwartz
secondary.rationale: A highly regarded scholarly biography and intellectual history of Confucius by a prominent sinologist.

secondary.title: The Analects: An Introduction
secondary.author: D.C. Lau
secondary.rationale: A foundational scholarly introduction and translation of the Analects, providing context and analysis.

secondary.title: Confucianism: A Very Short Introduction
secondary.author: Daniel A. Bell
secondary.rationale: A concise and accessible overview of Confucianism, its history, and its relevance, written by a leading scholar in the field.

suggestions.notes: The primary sources listed are foundational texts of Confucianism, attributed to Confucius and compiled by his disciples. Their exact authorship and dating are subject to scholarly debate, but they are universally considered primary in the study of Confucius. Secondary sources are chosen for their scholarly reputation and recency.
